edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 43,000,000 for the Shares, payable in immediately available funds at Closing, subject only to any escrow expressly provided in this Agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur on a date mutually agreed by the Buyer and the Seller, which date shall be as promptly as practicable after satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, including receipt of required third-party, regulatory, and internal approvals and completion of Buyer’s confirmatory due diligence to its reasonable satisfaction. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to satisfy the closing conditions promptly.

3. Representations and Warranties. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer that: (a) the Seller has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) the Seller owns good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws or this Agreement; (c) the Company’s capitalization is as disclosed to the Buyer; (d) the financial statements provided to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition of the Company for the periods covered; (e) except as disclosed to the Buyer, the Company has no material undisclosed liabilities; (f) the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws; (g) the Company has filed material tax returns required to be filed and paid material taxes due, except for taxes being contested in good faith; (h) material contracts, litigation, employee matters, and intellectual property matters are as disclosed to the Buyer; and (i) since the date of the most recent financial statements provided to the Buyer, there has been no material adverse change in the Company’s business, taken as a whole.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential and may not be disclosed except to the parties’ respective representatives, financing sources, and advisors who are informed of the confidential nature of the information, or as required by law. The confidentiality obligations in this Section shall survive termination of this Agreement and Closing.

5. Conditions to Closing. The Buyer’s obligation to close shall be subject to: (a) the Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct at Closing, except for inaccuracies that would not reasonably be expected to be material to the Company, taken as a whole; (b) the Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; (c) receipt of required third-party, regulatory, and internal approvals; and (d) completion of Buyer’s confirmatory due diligence to its reasonable satisfaction. The Seller’s obligation to close shall be subject to the Buyer’s performance in all material respects of its obligations required to be performed at or prior to Closing, including payment of the Purchase Price.

6. Indemnification; Escrow. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from breaches of the Seller’s representations, warranties, and covenants and for pre-closing taxes and liabilities of the Company, in each case subject to customary limitations, including survival periods, a deductible or basket, exclusions for disclosed matters, mitigation obligations, and an aggregate cap to be agreed. At Closing, USD 2,000,000 of the Purchase Price shall be deposited into escrow for a period of 12 months solely to secure the Seller’s indemnification obligations, pursuant to an escrow agreement reasonably acceptable to the parties.

receiver.requested_changes: Buyer requests that the draft be revised as follows: (1) reduce Purchase Price to USD 39,000,000; (2) specify that USD 4,000,000 of the Purchase Price will be placed in escrow for 18 months; (3) provide a 24-month general survival period for representations and warranties, with fundamental reps, tax matters, authority, title, capitalization, and fraud surviving for the applicable statute of limitations; (4) set Seller’s indemnity cap at 20% of the Purchase Price for general claims and 100% for fundamental reps, taxes, pre-closing liabilities, title/authority/capitalization, and fraud; (5) include a true deductible/basket of USD 250,000, after which Buyer may recover losses in excess of the basket; (6) clarify that exclusions for disclosed matters apply only to matters fairly disclosed in a specific disclosure schedule, not generally disclosed materials; (7) retain Buyer’s closing condition for confirmatory diligence to Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, including review of customer concentration, contracts, tax, employment, IP, litigation, and debt/liability matters; and (8) add ordinary-course interim operating covenants through Closing and a bring-down of all Seller representations at Closing, subject only to negotiated materiality standards.
receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for Seller’s revised draft. Buyer appreciates the movement on structure and the inclusion of closing conditions, expanded representations, indemnity, and an escrow concept.

That said, Seller’s USD 43,000,000 counterproposal remains above Buyer’s view of value given the still-limited diligence record and the number of material protection points left open, including escrow size, survival, caps, basket, exclusions, and the scope of retained closing protections. Buyer is prepared to move substantially from its prior position, but only as part of a complete package.

Buyer would be prepared to proceed on the following basis:

1. Purchase Price: USD 39,000,000.
2. Escrow: USD 4,000,000 for 18 months to secure Seller’s indemnity obligations.
3. Indemnity: 24-month survival for general reps; fundamental reps, tax, title, authority, capitalization, pre-closing liabilities, and fraud to survive through the applicable statute of limitations.
4. Cap: 20% of purchase price for general indemnity claims; 100% for fundamental reps, taxes, pre-closing liabilities, title/authority/capitalization, and fraud.
5. Basket: USD 250,000 true deductible, with recovery only for losses above the basket.
6. Disclosed matters: exclusions only for matters fairly and specifically disclosed in a disclosure schedule.
7. Closing conditions: Buyer’s confirmatory diligence condition to remain, including review of customer concentration, material contracts, tax, employment, IP, litigation, and debt/liability matters.
8. Interim covenants and bring-down: Company to operate in the ordinary course through Closing, and Seller’s representations to be brought down at Closing subject only to agreed materiality qualifiers.

If Seller can accept this package, Buyer is prepared to instruct us to turn a revised draft promptly and work toward signing on an expedited basis. This proposal is made as a package, and Buyer reserves all rights if the package is not accepted.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
